images.title: Which city is more crowded?
images.purpose: Shows the unit rate finder in its simplest state: people per sq. km in Delhi and Mumbai, drawn as dots in areas.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two rectangles side by side on a common baseline, each filled with evenly spread dots, a rate under each.
images.exact_structure: Left: one teal (#0072B2) outlined rectangle labelled Delhi above and 1484 sq. km inside its top edge, holding exactly 30 evenly spread teal dots. Right: one amber (#E69F00) outlined rectangle about 0.37 times the area of the left one, labelled Mumbai above and 550 sq. km inside its top edge, holding exactly 20 evenly spread amber dots, so its dots sit visibly closer together. Under the left rectangle: ≈ 20216 per sq. km; under the right one: ≈ 36364 per sq. km, this one inside a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box. A small key at the bottom: one dot and the text 1 dot = 1 million. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Compare by the rate for one unit: Mumbai has more people in each sq. km.
